writeup.headline: Mesa Labs rates Hold: strong share-price trend and reasonable valuation offset by slow growth.
writeup.thesis: Mesa Laboratories scores 61, a Hold, 4 points short of the Buy band. The strongest factor is trend (89): the price is 26.6% above its 200-day average, shares are up 71.5% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and they are 28.4 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation scores 76. In absolute terms, P/S of 2.9x and P/FCF of 13.9x are moderate, with an FCF yield 2.2 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is near the middle overall, and P/FCF is cheaper than at 47 of the last 61 month-ends. Growth is the weak spot at 33: TTM revenue growth is 3.0%, latest-quarter revenue growth is 1.0% year on year, and growth slowed by 1.6 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (61) pairs a 64.2% gross margin and a 21.2% FCF margin with a thin 9.0% operating margin, and the diluted share count is up 3.7% year on year.
key_risks: Revenue growth is slowing, with latest-quarter growth of 1.0% year on year.
FY27 guidance due with results on Nov 9 will reflect a lower Clinical Genomics revenue outlook.
Restructuring (about 40 roles cut, Hamburg exit) carries execution risk.
Share dilution: diluted share count up 3.7% year on year, with stock-based pay at 6.5% of revenue.
After a large run-up, the price is 7.7% below its 52-week high and could give back gains if momentum fades.
what_would_change: A 4-point score gain would reach Buy, for example from a pickup in revenue growth lifting the growth factor from 33.
November guidance showing cost savings outweighing lower Clinical Genomics revenue could improve news and growth scores.
A drop toward Sell (17 points away) would likely need the strong trend score of 89 to break down alongside weaker growth or quality.
Clearer debt figures would allow a balance sheet score, which could move the composite either way.
